introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2026, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, duration one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Énoncés recopiés tels qu'imprimés (fautes d'anglais comprises : « Hire Purchased Act », « Trade description Act », « The rewards ... is », « One of these business organisations are incorporated », « Tramps steamers » ; option 45 A sans point final).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 1, 11, 21, 39. 1 : certificate of origin et consular invoice se disputent la définition (clé visée b). 11 : énoncé tronqué, le principe visé est proximate cause (clé visée a). 21 : certificate of incorporation et can sue and be sued sont deux réponses défendables (clé visée d). 39 : uninsurable risks et non quantified risks proches (clé visée c).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A document signed by a representative of the country from which goods are sent is:

*Options as printed:* A) Consignment note.   B) Certificate of origin.   C) Pro forma invoice.   D) Consular invoice.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A certificate of origin is signed and stamped by an authorised body of the exporting country (for example the chamber of commerce) to confirm the country in which the goods were produced or manufactured. A consignment note travels with goods sent by road or rail and is made out by the sender, not signed by a representative of a country. A pro forma invoice is only a preview of the sale prepared by the seller. A consular invoice is certified by the consul of the importing country, so it is linked to the country to which the goods are sent, not the country from which they are sent.

**Intended answer: B (Certificate of origin).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The practice of selling goods in foreign markets cheaper than at home is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Dumping is the sale of goods in a foreign market at a price lower than the price in the home market (sometimes even below the cost of production), usually to remove surplus stock or to capture the foreign market. Smuggling is illegal entry of goods without paying duty. Under invoicing means declaring a value lower than the real value on the invoice to pay less duty. An auction sale is a sale to the highest bidder.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following accounts does NOT earn interest?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Deposit, savings and time (fixed) deposit accounts keep money for saving, so the bank pays interest to the customer. A current account is meant for daily payments by cheque, and withdrawals are frequent, so it normally earns no interest (the customer may even pay bank charges).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An unclean bill of lading means that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bill of lading is a receipt issued by the shipping company for goods loaded on a ship. It is *clean* when the goods were received in good condition. It is *unclean* (or claused) when the shipping company has written a remark on it that the goods, or their packing, were damaged or short when loaded. A buyer or bank may refuse an unclean bill of lading.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: There is a record of damaged goods.
It can be transferred to anybody.
It is not a document of title.

questions.enonce_markdown: A summary of financial transactions of a business at the bank is contained in a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bank statement is sent by the bank to its customer and lists the deposits, withdrawals, charges and balance on the customer's account over a period, so it summarises the business's transactions at the bank. A balance sheet and a trial balance are accounting records kept by the business itself. A statement of account is sent by a supplier to a customer to show the dealings between the two traders (not the bank).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An advertising medium that provides detailed information of goods is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A newspaper has space for long text, descriptions, prices and pictures, and the reader can keep it and read it again, so it gives detailed information about goods. Radio messages are short and pass quickly. Posters carry a short message to attract attention. Hand bills are small leaflets and carry limited information.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque is crossed so that it is paid:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two parallel lines drawn across the face of a cheque make it a crossed cheque. The bank must then pay the money only into a bank account and not in cash over the counter. This protects the drawer and payee if the cheque is lost or stolen, because the payment can be traced.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A trade restriction that limits the importation of the quantity of goods is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A quota is a limit placed by the government on the quantity (or value) of a good that may be imported in a given period. An embargo is a total ban on trade with a country or in a product. Export subsidies are payments to help exporters. Tariffs (import duties) are taxes on imported goods and limit imports by price, not by quantity.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Stock-turn means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Stock turnover (rate of stock turn) shows how many times a trader sells and replaces the average stock during a period, usually one year:

$$\text{Stock turnover}=\frac{\text{Cost of goods sold}}{\text{Average stock}}$$

So it is the number of times the *average stock* is sold. A high figure means goods sell quickly. Option A does not mention the average stock, and B and D do not describe a rate.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Number of times goods are sold.
Value of stocks in a shop.
Number of times average stock is sold.

questions.enonce_markdown: A shipping document showing details of goods in a ship is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A manifest is prepared by the shipping company (the master of the ship) and lists all the cargo carried on the ship, with the details of each consignment. It is shown to customs officers at the port. A bill of lading is a receipt for the goods of one shipper, a freight note states the freight charge, and a dock warrant is a document of title for goods stored in a dock warehouse (the printed "duck warrant" is read as dock warrant).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The principle that the risk insured must occur is:

*Options as printed:* A) Proximate cause.   B) Subrogation.   C) Contribution.   D) Utmost good faith.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sentence as printed is not clear. The principle that links a loss to the insured risk is *proximate cause*: the loss is paid only when the nearest and effective cause of the loss is the risk that was insured (for example fire in a fire policy). Subrogation lets the insurer take over the insured's rights after paying, contribution shares a claim between insurers, and utmost good faith requires full and true disclosure of facts.

**Intended answer: A (Proximate cause).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank service that enables a customer to withdraw money from his account at any time is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An automated teller machine (ATM) works 24 hours a day with the customer's card and PIN, so the customer can withdraw cash at any time. A night safe is used to deposit takings after banking hours. Credit transfer and direct debit are methods of paying money to another person or firm.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the cost price of goods is 400,000 CFAF and selling price is 500,000 CFAF, then mark-up is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mark-up is the profit expressed as a percentage of the cost price.

Profit = selling price - cost price = 500,000 - 400,000 = 100,000 CFAF.

$$\text{Mark-up}=\frac{100\,000}{400\,000}\times 100=25\%$$

The trap is option C (20%), which is the margin: profit divided by the selling price, $\frac{100\,000}{500\,000}\times 100=20\%$.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Hire purchase is a form of credit sales most convenient in the sale of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Under hire purchase the buyer pays a deposit, takes the goods at once and pays the balance by instalments; ownership passes only after the last instalment. It suits expensive goods that last a long time, called durable goods (cars, refrigerators, furniture), because the buyer uses them while paying. Non-durable goods (food, soap) are used up quickly and are bought for cash.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main purpose of a delivery note is to Acknowledge:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A delivery note goes with the goods. The buyer checks the goods against it and signs a copy, which is returned to the seller. The signature acknowledges that the goods have been *received*, and it is the seller's proof that they were delivered. It does not show payment or the means of transport.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The means of transport used in delivery.

questions.enonce_markdown: A shop with several stores under one roof is a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A department store is a large shop divided into departments (clothes, shoes, furniture, electrical goods and so on) under one roof, each department managed separately. A multiple shop is a chain of similar shops in many towns. A supermarket is a large self-service shop selling mainly food and household goods. A hypermarket is a very large self-service store, usually outside the town centre.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The advertising medium that combines sound and images is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Television shows moving pictures together with sound, so it combines sound and images. Radio has sound only, while posters and newspapers have images and print only.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a hire purchase transaction, 25,000 CFAF is paid as deposit and the remainder paid in five equal installments of 30,000 CFAF. What is the hire purchase price?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hire purchase price = deposit + total of the instalments.

Instalments = 5 x 30,000 = 150,000 CFAF.

Hire purchase price = 25,000 + 150,000 = 175,000 CFAF.

The trap is option B (150,000 CFAF), which forgets the deposit.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document showing details of money collected from the bank is a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A withdrawal slip is filled in by the customer to take money out of his account at the counter; it shows the account, the amount and the signature. A cheque is an order to pay a named person, a standing order form instructs the bank to make regular payments, and a bank statement lists past transactions.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Act of Parliament that prevents the payments for goods not ordered for is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Unsolicited goods are goods sent to a person who has not asked for them. The law that protects consumers in this case is the Unsolicited Goods and Services Act: the receiver is not obliged to pay for the goods or to return them. The Hire Purchase Act protects buyers on credit, and the Trade Descriptions Act forbids false descriptions of goods and services.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An enterprise is a separate legal entity because it:

*Options as printed:* A) Produces goods.   B) Is financially independent.   C) Has a certificate of incorporation.   D) Can sue and be sued.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A separate legal entity (a legal person) is distinct from its owners. Two options can be defended: it receives this status when it is registered and obtains a certificate of incorporation, and because of this status it can own property, sue and be sued in its own name. Producing goods and being financially independent are not what gives the legal status.

**Intended answer: D (Can sue and be sued).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The rewards for capital as a factor of production is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The four factors of production and their rewards are: land - rent; labour - wages; capital - interest; entrepreneur - profit.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One of these business organisations are incorporated:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An incorporated business is registered as a separate legal person. Joint stock companies (private and public limited companies) are incorporated: they have a certificate of incorporation, they can sue and be sued, and their shareholders have limited liability. A sole proprietor and an ordinary partnership are unincorporated, because the owners and the business are one in law.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Loss leaders are operated in order to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A loss leader is a product sold at or below cost price by a shop. The shop accepts a loss on this product so that customers come in, and the shop hopes they will also buy other goods at normal prices and earn a profit on them. The aim is therefore to attract customers.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most flexible means of transport is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Road transport can serve almost any place, door to door, at any time, with vehicles of many sizes. Rail is limited to tracks and stations, sea to ports and air to airports.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following bank services is suitable in paying monthly rents?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A standing order is an instruction from the customer to the bank to pay a fixed amount to a named person on fixed dates (for example 100,000 CFAF on the 1st of each month), which is exactly the case of a rent that is the same every month. A direct debit is for amounts that change and is started by the receiver, a bank draft is used for one single payment, and a crossed cheque must be written each time.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The insurance principle that an insured must follow when filling the proposal form is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The proposal form is the form in which the person who wants insurance gives the facts about himself and the risk. The principle of utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) requires him to tell the truth and disclose all material facts; if he hides a fact, the insurer may refuse to pay a claim. Contribution, insurable interest and proximate cause apply to the policy and the claim.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are ancillaries to trade EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Aids (ancillaries) to trade are services that help trade to run smoothly: banking, transport, insurance, warehousing, communication and advertising. Retailers are traders who buy from wholesalers and sell to consumers, so they belong to trade itself and are not an aid to trade.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A multiple shop can NOT be identified with which of the following?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A multiple shop (chain store) has many branches in different towns, a central warehouse that supplies them and the same appearance and name. It buys in large quantities and normally sells for cash at low prices; it does not sell on credit. So selling on credit does not identify it.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Speed is a characteristic to be considered when choosing a means of transport when goods are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Perishable goods (fresh fish, fruit, meat, flowers) go bad quickly, so they need a fast means of transport such as air or refrigerated road transport. Heavy and bulky goods are chosen for cost and capacity (rail or sea), and light goods have no special need for speed.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term 'limited liability' means that shareholders are:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Limited liability means that if the company cannot pay its debts, each shareholder can lose only the amount that he has invested (or promised to invest) in shares. His personal property cannot be taken to pay the company's debts. Options B and D describe unlimited liability, and A is wrong because a shareholder can lose the capital contributed.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Responsible for business debts up to their personal property.
Liable to business debts up to capital contributed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Commerce is subdivided into:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Commerce is made of two branches: trade (buying and selling of goods, both at home and abroad) and aids to trade (banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication and advertising).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document showing details of a single trade transaction is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An invoice is sent by the seller to the buyer for one sale. It shows the goods, quantity, price, discounts and total amount to pay. A statement of account summarises many transactions over a period, a bank statement shows the account at the bank, and a pro forma invoice is a preview before a sale is agreed.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An order to an agent abroad to buy from a specific manufacturer is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An indent is an order sent by an importer to an agent abroad (an indent house) asking him to buy goods. A *closed indent* names the manufacturer or supplier from whom the agent must buy. In an *open indent* the agent chooses the supplier.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mail service offered to tourists in a town is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Post restante (poste restante) is a post office service that keeps letters until the person, who has no fixed address in the town, comes to collect them, which suits tourists. Express post is a fast delivery, data post carries business data and recorded delivery gives proof of posting and delivery.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Capital used for the day-to-day running of the business is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Working capital is the money available to pay daily expenses such as stock, wages and electricity (current assets minus current liabilities). Fixed capital is invested in long-lasting assets such as buildings and machines. Capital employed is the total long-term funds in the business. Circulating capital is another name that is often used for current assets, but the standard term for the funds used in daily running is working capital.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Act of Parliament that ensures that goods purchased meet the purpose for which they were bought is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Sale of Goods Act says that goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for the purpose for which they are bought and as described by the seller. The Trade Descriptions Act deals with false descriptions of goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The rate of exchange of a country's exports to imports is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The terms of trade compare the prices a country gets for its exports with the prices it pays for its imports (an index of export prices over import prices). Balance of trade is the difference between the value of exports and imports, the exchange rate is the price of one currency in another and the balance of payments is the full record of money flows with other countries.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Risks that do not have existing statistics are known as:

*Options as printed:* A) Insurable risks.   B) Insurable interest.   C) Uninsurable risks.   D) Non quantified risks.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An insurer fixes a premium from statistics on how often a loss happens, so a risk without statistics cannot be priced and is not accepted: it is an uninsurable risk (for example the risk of a new business making a loss). Insurable interest is not a type of risk. Option D is not a standard term in the syllabus.

**Intended answer: C (Uninsurable risks).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The oldest function of commercial banks is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first and oldest function of a bank is to accept deposits, that is to keep the money of customers safely. The banks use these deposits to give loans, and the other services (night safe, payment of standing orders) came later.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a special purpose ship?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A special purpose ship is built to carry one kind of cargo: tankers (oil and liquids), refrigerated ships or car carriers. Tramp steamers have no fixed route or timetable, and ocean and coastal liners sail regularly on fixed routes carrying general cargo and passengers.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent that prepares documents for shipment of goods is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A forwarding agent arranges the transport of goods for exporters: he prepares and handles the shipping documents, deals with customs and books space on the ship. A del credere agent guarantees the customer's payment for an extra commission, a broker brings buyers and sellers together without holding the goods, and a factor holds the goods and sells them in his own name.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Trade is subdivided into:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade is the buying and selling of goods. It is divided according to the place where it takes place: home trade (within the country, also called domestic or internal trade) and foreign trade (between countries). Retailing and wholesaling are the two parts of home trade, and export and import are the two parts of foreign trade.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Buying and selling within the country is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Domestic trade (home trade) is buying and selling inside the borders of one country, for example a Douala wholesaler selling to a retailer in Yaounde. International and foreign trade take place between countries, and entrepôt trade is the import of goods in order to export them again.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The department of an enterprise responsible for procurement and supplies is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Procurement means obtaining the goods, materials and supplies that the enterprise needs. This is the work of the purchasing department, which finds suppliers, asks for quotations, places orders and checks the deliveries. Personnel deals with staff, accounting with money records and production with making goods.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Democratic control is common in which of these business units?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a co-operative society every member has one vote, whatever the number of shares or the money invested (one man, one vote), so control is democratic. In companies the votes follow the number of shares held.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An internal source of capital to a partnership business is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Internal sources come from the owners themselves: the partners' own savings, their contributions and the profits kept in the business. Loans and trade credit come from outside persons or firms, and a partnership cannot sell shares to the public (this is done by companies).

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A summary of business transactions within a given trade period is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A statement of account is sent by a seller to a customer, usually each month. It lists the invoices, credit notes and payments of the period and shows the balance still owed. An invoice covers one transaction, a pro forma invoice is a preview and a balance sheet shows the assets and liabilities at one date.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following services are provided to retailers by the wholesaler EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The wholesaler buys in bulk from producers and breaks the bulk into smaller lots that retailers can afford, so selling in small quantities is a service to retailers. He also stores goods (warehousing) so that retailers do not need big stores, and he supplies a wide variety of goods in one place. Selling in bulk is the way the wholesaler buys from producers and is not a service given to retailers, who need small lots.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT involved in E-Banking?
questions.corrige_markdown:
E-banking uses electronic means: ATM, debit and credit cards, internet and mobile banking. A cheque is a paper document written and signed by hand and is processed through clearing, so it is not electronic banking.

**Answer: C.**
